newsitem.title: UK: Brady bonds continue higher on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds continue higher on Greenspan comments.

text.p: Brady bond prices stormed ahead on Wednesday on growing expectations the Federal Reserve would keep U.S. monetary policy on hold for the remainder of the year, traders said on Wednesday.

"At the moment, no one is worried about currency problems and people are buying back their positions that they sold in the last couple of months," said one Brady bond trader at a U.S. investment bank in London.
Dollar-denominated Brady assets continued to climb on comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Tuesday on his first day of Humprhey Hawkins testimony to U.S. Congress.
Greenspan, in his first leg of testimony to the House Banking Committee, said U.S. economic growth was slowing for now and that inflation in 1997 would be quite modest.

U.S. financial markets interpreted the Fed Chief's comments to mean U.S. monetary policy was on hold for the time being. The comments fuelled a spectacular rally in the U.S. Treasury market, pushing the yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond to 6.42 percent, its lowest closing level since December 5, 1996.
Among the Eastern European instruments, Russian dollar-denominated Vneshekonombank loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were one point higher at 94-3/8 bid and Bulgarian Iabs BGFLTH11=RR were 7/8 higher at 76 bid.
In the Latin Brady market, Mexican par bonds MX625L19=RR were 3/8 higher at 81-1/4 bid and Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were 1/4 firmer at 74 bid.
